name: Vorrathine
description: Vorrathine is a dual-action compound that combines aggressive dopaminergic stimulation with targeted prefrontal cortex suppression, chemically dismantling the higher reasoning functions that produce hesitation, moral calculation, and threat-assessment doubt. The result is a combatant operating almost entirely on limbic-system aggression: faster decisions, no retreat instinct, no calculation of odds. Nightshade sells it legally as a 'combat performance aid' with a prescription label; its actual market is anyone who needs to stop thinking and start killing.
effects: Suppression of prefrontal hesitation and moral reasoning
Tunnel-vision focus on immediate physical threats
side_effects: Complete inability to distinguish friend from foe at peak effect
Blackout periods — users frequently cannot recall actions taken
High risk of committing violence against allies
Documented cases of users continuing to attack after sustaining fatal injuries
cultural_context: Vorrathine is the drug that responsible runners don't take on team ops. It is popular in gang warfare on the Shelf because it is cheap and terrifying — a single Vorra-dosed fighter can break a defensive line through sheer overwhelming aggression. It is also the reason experienced mercenaries refuse certain contracts: 'Vorra territory' is a phrase that means the tactical situation has devolved beyond rational combat. Nightshade's legal fig leaf is threadbare, and Lazarus has lobbied twice to have it reclassified as illegal.
story_hooks: A gang war on the Shelf has escalated to catastrophic civilian casualties because one faction started dosing their fighters with Vorrathine — someone needs to cut the supply line before the Shelf becomes a killzone.
A Nightshade executive is using Vorrathine in closed clinical trials on Shelf residents recruited under false pretenses; the data they're collecting suggests a more controllable reformulation.
A runner wakes up in an alley with blood on her hands and no memory of the last two hours — she doesn't use Vorrathine, but someone may have dosed her without consent.
